messages:
maria gonzalez: quick sync — product flagged some client errors coming back from /v1/generate. we currently return 422 for prompt>limit, 500 for infra blips. product thinks 422 feels odd for 'length' and prefers 400 or 413. which should we standardize on? also want clear guidance on retryability.

devon li: iirc 413 is technically payload too large (http semantics) — useful when clients send huge byte payloads. 422 is 'unprocessable entity' (semantic validation). 400 is generic bad request (malformed). i'd map like: 400 = invalid JSON/params, 413 = payload exceeds server limits, 422 = business-level validation (e.g., instructions missing), 5xx = transient infra.

samir patel: +1 to devon's mapping. practical example: if prompt tokens > model max -> 413 (not retryable). if prompt contains disallowed content -> 422 (client must change). if model runtime OOM -> 502/503 (retryable).

kevin ng: what about streaming endpoints? midstream validation vs post-init? e.g. streaming generates, then a plugin call fails. do we send a terminal error frame or a 5xx?

samir patel: for streaming, prefer terminal error frames with structured error payload and final status code in metadata. clients that consume stream should treat terminal frames as final (no implicit retry). For recoverable infra we can include an envelope like: {"type":"error","code":502,"retryable":true,"message":"gpu OOM, retry with backoff"}.

jess harrington: compatibility note — if we switch 422->413 for existing cases, that's breaking for clients that parse codes. can we do a rollout: accept both codes for a couple weeks and surface warnings in console? also add docs and sample client logic.

api-bot: buildkite:pr/432 schema-check found: new error-code mapping in api-spec.json -> flagged as potentially breaking.

maria gonzalez: thanks — plan proposal: 1) spec PR that clearly lists canonical mapping + examples, 2) make server accept dual codes (422 or 413) for one release and emit a deprecation header when sending legacy code, 3) add client snippet in docs for retry guidance. who can own the spec PR?

devon li: i'll own the PR. i'll add a short decision table and examples. will link here when ready.

jess harrington: also please add a tiny section on idempotency keys for generate calls where we recommend clients set one for any retryable 5xx responses.

devon li: draft snippet i'll add to docs: 
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "MODEL_OOM",
    "http_status": 502,
    "message": "model OOM on server",
    "retryable": true,
    "retry_after": 2
  }
}
```
and header: `Retry-After: 2` (seconds) for 5xxs where we can estimate. for 413/422/400 -> `retryable=false`.

samir patel: tiny nuance: some clients do optimistic retry on 429 with exponential backoff — include that in the retry table. 429 -> retryable with 'Retry-After' or backoff. 5xx -> retryable; 4xx -> not (except maybe 409 conflict idempotency flows).

maria gonzalez: perfect. devon, add canary toggle and deprecation header `X-Deprecated-Error: 422` when we still emit old 422. jess/law/security: please flag if this affects compliance.

devon li: will do. PR link when up: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-api/pull/432> (draft).

jess harrington: adding a quick client example for node in the PR would help: show 5xx retry loop + idempotency header.

maria gonzalez: ok thanks everyone — assigning follow-ups: devon PR owner, samir to update stream terminal error docs, jess to review client guidance. loop back in 48h. :thumbsup:

kevin ng: acked. will watch canary logs and surface any anomalies.

api-bot: deploy-canary: service/generate -> canary rollout started (10%)

maria gonzalez: closing out thread — will file a short ops runbook entry once PR merges.
